beats.subline: Thursday, September 17, 2026 close — stocks rallied as bond yields and oil prices eased in the wake of the Fed's rate hike.
beats.body: Wall Street bounced back from Wednesday's Fed-driven selloff as the 10-year Treasury yield retreated and Brent crude fell to roughly $104 a barrel after the Energy Secretary said Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline -- an alternative route for oil stuck behind the Strait of Hormuz blockade -- would be restored soon; tech led the gains, with the Nasdaq outperforming.

beats.headline: Trump says the US is 'hopefully toward the end' of the Iran war, claims direct contact with Tehran
beats.body: President Trump said Wednesday that Iran had reached out to the US directly and was seeking a deal, raising the prospect of renewed diplomacy after seven months of war, but a senior Iranian security official accused him of sending 'mixed signals' and said Tehran would not negotiate until its conditions are met.

beats.headline: Rubio and Wang Yi hold call to finalize agenda for Xi's September 24 Washington summit
beats.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke Thursday to shape an agenda expected to cover trade, AI governance, and military-to-military ties ahead of Xi Jinping's visit next week, where Trump plans to personally greet him on arrival -- a courtesy not extended to other leaders this term. Asian allies remain worried Trump could soften US support for Taiwan in exchange for economic concessions.

beats.headline: Tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' in Strait of Hormuz, fire extinguished
beats.body: The UK Maritime Trade Operations center said a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was hit early Friday, sparking a fire that crew later extinguished with no reported injuries; UKMTO did not identify the vessel or assign responsibility, the latest in a string of incidents disrupting shipping through the corridor since the naval blockade began.

beats.headline: Air Force says Boeing's F-47 stealth fighter remains on track for a 2028 first flight
beats.body: Gen. Dale White, the Pentagon's director of Critical Major Weapons Systems, said the sixth-generation F-47 program has cleared its technology-maturation and risk-reduction work and 'we see no issues in front of us right now' toward flying within this administration; the jet, which beat out a Lockheed Martin bid in March 2025, will replace the F-22 with a planned buy of 185-200 aircraft.

beats.headline: Anthropic says Claude now leads 26% of the company's own AI research and development
beats.body: Anthropic said Claude autonomously leads about a quarter of its research and development work -- completing tasks end-to-end from a high-level prompt under human supervision -- up from essentially zero in February, while roughly 90% of R&D is done in close collaboration with the model; the announcement comes as Anthropic prepares for a planned IPO this fall.

beats.headline: Darnell Wright returns to limited practice Thursday after sitting out with a knee injury
beats.body: The Bears' All-Pro right tackle, who missed Wednesday's session, was back at Halas Hall in a limited role Thursday wearing sleeves on both legs but no hard brace; the team said it will monitor his response at Friday's practice before settling his designation for Sunday's home opener against the Vikings.
